## Research question

Repeated clarification can revisit plausible meanings while missing the database columns or values required by the intended interpretation.

## Method

Constructs candidate column pairs from semantic, name and value signals, then uses an LLM to annotate potential ambiguity conditions. First-turn retrieval combines graph neighbors and MinHash value matches, prunes alternatives, and generates a clarification batch. Later turns use Sphinteract's output/question taxonomy.

## Evaluation

Uses 1,534 BIRD-dev questions, primarily without supplied evidence, a shared seed parser, corrected single references and a gold-informed Qwen user simulator. Reports column-order-insensitive execution matching, reference-column precision/recall and system-side trajectory tokens. Ablations vary graph construction, retrieval, model size and supplied evidence.

## What the results support

At four turns, Bridge reports 77.38% execution matching versus Sphinteract's 65.78% at comparable token cost; Sphinteract's ten-turn result is 69.82%. Graph and trigger-context ablations reduce accuracy. Gains remain smaller when BIRD evidence is supplied.

## Limits and qualifications

Evaluation assumes rejected predictions can be identified and simulated users know the gold SQL. Multiple-gold ambiguity corrections are excluded; wrong-column failures are only a proxy for ambiguity. Token accounting excludes user simulation and does not establish total deployment cost. No real-user or unanswerability evaluation is reported; graph maintenance under database changes remains future work.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

Provides concrete database-grounded clarification cues and controlled component comparisons, with conditional correction results rather than general ambiguity-detection guarantees.
